zh.summary: 將「更有效率」拆成可觀察指標，標明假設與資料來源，讓需求變更、測試證據和下一步決定可以相互追溯。
objectives: 為功能結果與使用者任務各定義可觀察的成功條件。
為指標寫出分母、量測方法、基準與適用範圍。
將假設、需求候選、確認決定及修訂理由接回 problem.md。

readingGuide.goal: 為功能結果與使用者任務各定義可觀察的成功條件。
readingGuide.startingPoint: problem.md、文字編輯器與本章合成算例；不收集真人成績或計時。
readingGuide.route: 先看情境與原理，再比較例子，最後擴寫 problem.md 並用檢核題自查。
readingGuide.output: problem.md 有可重做的指標定義、假設、需求候選與變更紀錄，結果欄如實保留未測量。

sections.heading: 做出功能之後，如何判定真的有用？
paragraphs: 這一課非常重要，因為它決定了你做出來的系統，究竟只是「能夠運作」，還是「真的解決了問題」。
先記住一句話：做出功能不等於達成目標；達成目標必須有證據，而證據必須事先定義怎麼取得。
想像你花了一個月開發 AI 系統，最後向主管報告：
「我們完成了 20 個功能、寫了 10,000 行程式碼，而且 AI 可以自動產生報告！」
主管可能只問一句：
「所以，原本需要半小時的工作，現在到底快了多少？錯誤有沒有減少？」
這就是今天要學的核心。

sections.heading: 一、先建立完整觀念：從需求到證據
paragraphs: 我們先把整個軟體開發流程串起來。

blocks.caption: 圖 1｜從問題到決策
blocks.description: 六步呈現需求、設計假設、指標與證據的關係；證據仍可能要求回頭修正。

items.title: 1. Problem｜問題
items.body: 使用者經常漏填資料，導致報告錯誤

items.title: 2. Requirement｜需求
items.body: 資料缺漏時，系統不得匯出完整報告

items.title: 3. Hypothesis｜假設
items.body: 告訴使用者缺少什麼，就可能讓他自行修正

items.title: 4. Metric｜成功指標
items.body: 缺漏阻擋率、無提示完成率、完成時間

items.title: 5. Evidence｜測試證據
items.body: 測試紀錄、實際操作結果、錯誤案例

items.title: 6. Decision｜決策
items.body: 通過驗收、修正設計，或重新檢查需求

paragraphs: 其中最需要理解的是：需求說明系統應該做什麼；假設解釋為什麼這樣設計可能有效；指標則定義如何判斷結果。
三者不能混為一談。

sections.heading: 二、功能指標與任務指標：機器成功，不等於人成功
paragraphs: 假設你開發一個「AI 文件收件系統」。
使用者上傳文件後，系統會檢查有沒有缺件，最後產生報告。
現在你想知道它做得好不好。
這時需要兩個不同角度。

blocks.caption: 圖 2｜功能指標與任務指標
blocks.description: 兩種指標分開取得證據，彼此補充。

items.title: 功能指標（Functional Metric）
items.body:
系統有沒有依照預先設定的規則正確運作？

例如：缺件時是否阻擋匯出？修改資料後，是否要求重新檢查？

驗證方式通常是自動化測試、人工操作測試。

items.title: 任務指標（Task Metric）
items.body:
使用者能不能順利完成真正想做的事情？

例如：第一次使用的人，能否自己找到缺漏、補齊資料、取得正確報告？

驗證方式可能是使用者任務測試、計時、觀察操作過程。

paragraphs: 這兩種指標為什麼一定要分開？
想像系統設計出一個「檢查缺漏」按鈕。
工程師測試後發現，每次按下去都能正確檢查，功能指標達到 100%。
但實際使用者根本不知道這個按鈕在哪裡。
那麼：

- 從工程角度，這項功能可能通過測試。
- 從使用者角度，任務仍然可能失敗。
反過來也一樣。使用者成功產生一份報告，不表示系統已經通過所有安全與例外情境的檢查。
一個好系統，要同時證明「做得對」與「用得成」。

sections.heading: 三、成功指標怎麼算？分母是關鍵
paragraphs: 現在我們來實際計算。
假設總共有六筆合成測試資料，其中四筆缺漏，兩筆完整。
我們想衡量的叫「缺漏阻擋率」。
公式：缺漏阻擋率＝成功阻擋的缺漏案例／全部缺漏案例 × 100%。

blocks.caption: 圖 3｜互動練習：改變成功阻擋數，看看結果
blocks.description: 四筆缺漏的固定合成案例；結果只供練習計算，不是實際測試證據。

items.title: 未達本版阻擋要求
items.body: 本版要求 4 / 4 全數阻擋

items.title: 判讀
items.body: 還有 1 筆缺漏案例沒有成功阻擋，不能因其他正常案例成功，就宣稱這項規則已經通過。

sections.heading: 分母、零案例與錯誤阻擋
paragraphs: 這裡有三個值得記住的地方。
第一，分母必須是你真正想研究的對象。 我們研究的是「缺漏能不能被擋住」，因此只看四筆缺漏資料，而不是全部六筆。
第二，百分比不能取代原始數量。 75% 聽起來好像還可以，但寫成 3/4，就會發現四筆裡有一筆漏擋。對這個特定驗收要求而言，它是失敗的。
第三，沒有測試，不代表成功。 假如這次根本沒有缺漏案例，分母就是零，無法計算阻擋率。應記錄「未測得／不適用」，而不是寫 100%。
還有一個容易忽略的陷阱：系統如果把六筆資料全部擋住，缺漏阻擋率也會是 100%，但正常資料根本不能完成工作。
所以，實務上還需要搭配「完整資料能否正確匯出」等功能測試，避免只把一個指標做到漂亮。

sections.heading: 四、怎麼證明使用者真的比較快？
paragraphs: 假設 AI 系統宣稱：
「使用我們的產品，產製一份報告可以節省五分鐘。」
你第一個應該問的是：
這五分鐘怎麼量出來的？
想像兩種測量方式。

blocks.caption: 圖 4｜先核對計時起點
blocks.description: 15 與 10 分鐘是不同計時範圍的示意，不能據此認定節省五分鐘。

items.title: 舊流程
items.body:
15 分鐘

從打開文件、整理資料開始計時

items.title: 新流程
items.body:
10 分鐘

從資料整理完成、按下產生按鈕才計時

paragraphs: 看起來節省五分鐘，但兩個流程的計時起點不同。
這個比較就不公平。
比較時，應盡可能做到相同的任務、同等難度的資料、相同起終點，並記錄使用者是否得到額外協助。
例如統一定義：
「從使用者第一次看到指定資料開始，到成功取得與當前資料相符的正確報告為止。」
但即使這樣，也要注意：
假設使用者第一次操作舊系統，第二次操作新系統，他可能只是因為已經熟悉任務，所以做得更快。
這叫做練習效應（Practice Effect）。
因此，一次測量到的時間差，不足以證明改善一定由新系統造成。較嚴謹的比較可以考慮讓不同參與者交換操作順序，或使用難度相當的不同題目。
而且，只計算成功者的完成時間也有問題。如果有一半的人放棄了，就不能只報另一半成功者的平均時間，卻不揭露失敗率。

sections.heading: 五、假設（Hypothesis）：你相信的事情，不一定是真的
paragraphs: 這個觀念在 AI 開發中尤其重要。
例如，你想讓使用者自行修正資料，因此你設計了一個功能：
「當資料缺漏時，畫面顯示缺少的欄位名稱。」
你認為這樣能讓使用者自己補齊資料。
但請注意：
這是設計假設，還不是已經證實的事實。
它可能因為幾種原因而失敗。
使用者可能看不懂欄位的意思；可能知道缺少什麼，卻不知道去哪裡拿；也可能知道資料在哪裡，但沒有權限取得。
你應該把原本的想法轉換成可以驗證的敘述。

blocks.caption: 表 2
rows: 明確列出缺漏欄位，能幫助使用者自行修正
讓使用者在不接受提示下完成指定補件任務
無提示完成率、卡住的位置與原因
使用者看懂提示，仍反覆無法找到資料來源
訪談資料取得流程，或改善提示設計

paragraphs: 最有價值的是「反證條件」。
它在問：
什麼結果出現時，我願意承認原本的想法需要修改？
這也是科學研究和工程驗證的重要共同點。
在研究論文中，你提出 Hypothesis，安排實驗取得 Evidence，最後才形成 Conclusion。
在軟體工程中也是一樣，只是證據可能來自功能測試、使用者任務測試或實際營運資料。

sections.heading: 六、需求紀錄：為什麼不能隨便改掉原本的要求？
paragraphs: 現在進入最後一個關鍵觀念：Traceability（可追溯性）。
想像一個開發情境。
原始需求寫著：
「使用者完成資料檢查後，可以匯出報告。」
工程師已經完成這個功能。
可是測試時發現一個問題。

blocks.caption: 圖 5｜過期檢查結果的問題
blocks.description: 設計風險；最後的補充規則是針對風險的需求，驗收證據仍待取得。

items.title: 1. 檢查資料 A
items.body: 使用者輸入資料 A，按下檢查，系統顯示通過。

items.title: 2. 修改成資料 B
items.body: 使用者又修改了資料，變成資料 B。

items.title: 3. 沿用舊狀態
items.body: 系統卻保留資料 A 的「檢查通過」狀態。

items.title: 4. 未重新檢查就匯出
items.body: 使用者直接匯出資料 B 的報告，沒有重新檢查。

items.title: 應補充的規則
items.body: 每當影響檢查結果的輸入資料改變時，原本的檢查通過狀態必須失效，重新檢查後才能完整匯出。

paragraphs: 這個問題非常典型。
原本的需求不一定寫錯，但它不夠完整。
因此，不能只是悄悄把原始需求改掉，而是應該記錄：

blocks.caption: 表 3
rows: 明確提示缺漏，有助於使用者自行修正
指定缺漏案例必須全數阻擋
輸入修改後，先前檢查結果失效
發現可能使用過期檢查結果匯出

paragraphs: 這個表格有什麼價值？
三個月後，新工程師可能問：「為什麼每次修改資料，都一定要重新檢查？」
有了紀錄，你可以指出原始需求、發現的風險、決策理由，以及驗證這項規則的測試。
這就是需求可追溯性。它不只是文件管理，更是讓系統長期可維護的重要工程能力。
H、M、R、C 只是教材示範的分類代號，不是強制使用的標準。

sections.heading: 七、實務上怎麼運用？一張表就能開始
paragraphs: 在實際開發 MVP 時，不一定需要導入大型需求管理系統。
可以先用 Markdown 建立 `problem.md`，把最重要的資訊放在一起。
這裡提供一份精簡示範：

blocks.heading: problem.md
paragraphs: 合成範例；結果保持未測量。
blocks.code:
# AI 文件收件系統

## 問題
使用者常因資料缺漏，產生不完整報告。

## 需求 R-01
缺件時不得完整匯出報告。

## 假設 H-01
顯示缺漏欄位可以協助使用者自行修正。

狀態：尚未驗證

## 功能指標 M-01
名稱：缺漏阻擋率
公式：阻擋成功數 / 指定缺漏案例數
要求：指定案例全數阻擋
結果：未測量

## 任務指標 M-02
名稱：無提示完成率
公式：無提示完成者 / 開始任務者
結果：未測量

## 變更 C-01
修改輸入後，舊檢查結果必須失效。

理由：避免以過期結果匯出。

## 待補證據
- 功能測試結果
- 使用者測試紀錄
- 驗收決策

paragraphs: 注意這份文件最有價值的地方，不是它有多少欄位。
而是任何人打開，都能知道：
「我們要解決什麼問題？目前相信什麼？怎麼判定成功？實際驗證到什麼程度？為什麼要改？」
這樣的文件才能真正支援開發、驗收與維護。

sections.heading: 八、把今天學的東西放進更大的工程觀念
paragraphs: 你可以把 M03-05 視為連接「需求工程」與「軟體測試」的一座橋。

blocks.caption: 表 4
rows: 為什麼這樣設計可能有效？
怎麼判斷它有沒有做好？
怎麼知道每項規則從哪裡來？
發現不符合預期時怎麼辦？

paragraphs: 其中需要特別區分三個常被混淆的詞：
Verification（驗證是否符合規格）：我們有沒有把系統按照要求做對？
Validation（確認是否滿足真實需求）：我們做出來的東西，是否真的適合使用者要完成的工作？
Evaluation（評估）：透過既定指標與方法，衡量系統表現及其限制。
例如，系統能夠正確辨識缺漏，屬於重要的 Verification 證據；使用者能靠它順利完成補件工作，則能提供 Validation 證據。
兩者相互補充，但都不能靠空口宣稱。

sections.heading: 九、今天的理解測驗
paragraphs: 以下是新的合成情境，請先自己作答；本節先保留問題，參考答案可在下方「理解檢核與參考解析」展開。
一家醫院正在測試 AI 文件檢查系統。
工程師準備了五筆缺漏案例，其中四筆被成功阻擋，另一筆卻仍然可以匯出。
另外，四名參與者開始使用系統，其中兩人自行完成、一人需要工作人員提示、一人放棄。
專案經理宣稱：「我們預計讓每位使用者節省八分鐘，所以系統已經具備上線價值。」
請回答：

1. 這次的缺漏阻擋率是多少？如果驗收要求是指定缺漏案例全數阻擋，能否通過？
2. 無提示完成率是多少？需要提示的使用者應不應該算入分母？
3. 「節省八分鐘」目前屬於假設、已測量結果，還是正式結論？要怎麼驗證？
4. 如果發現修改資料後，系統仍使用舊的檢查結果，你會新增什麼需求？要保留哪些變更紀錄？
本課最終重點：成功不是你做了多少事情，而是你能拿出多少可靠、適切的證據，證明真正的問題已經獲得改善。
下一課 M04-01 會開始學習 HCI、UI 與 UX。你會發現今天的「使用者能否完成任務」，正是後續使用者體驗設計與可用性測試的重要基礎。

exercise.environment: problem.md、文字編輯器與本章合成算例；不收集真人成績或計時。
steps: 選一項功能指標與一項任務指標，各寫分母、起終點、資料來源與未測量欄位。
用四筆缺漏、三筆阻擋的合成卡計算，再解釋為何完整案例不進該分母；另處理分母為零。
新增 H-01、R-01 與一筆變更，保留來源、確認角色與理由，請同儕指出下一個仍待驗證的主張。
exercise.expected: problem.md 有可重做的指標定義、假設、需求候選與變更紀錄，結果欄如實保留未測量。
exercise.check: 能算出 3／4＝75% 並判定本版缺漏阻擋要求未通過；不把合成算例當真人或實際軟體結果。
exercise.cleanup: 保留合成標記與原始定義，不公開真人任務記錄；未測量項目保持未測量。

openChecks.prompt: 這次的缺漏阻擋率是多少？能否通過全數阻擋要求？
answer: 4／5＝80%。仍有一筆缺漏錯誤放行，未達指定缺漏案例全數阻擋要求。

openChecks.prompt: 無提示完成率是多少？需要提示者是否在分母？
answer: 2／4＝50%。分母是開始任務的四人，包含需要提示與放棄者；需要提示者不列入無提示完成的分子。

openChecks.prompt: 「節省八分鐘」是何種狀態？如何驗證？
answer: 目前是預期改善的假設，尚無量測結果。固定任務、同等難度資料與起終點，記錄提示、失敗和放棄，考慮交換操作順序以處理練習效應，再比較基準與新流程。

openChecks.prompt: 修改資料後仍沿用舊結果時，要加什麼規則與紀錄？
answer: 影響檢查的輸入一改變，舊通過結果便失效，重新檢查後才能完整匯出。保留原需求、C-01、變更理由、來源與決策，以及尚待取得的驗收證據；實測後再回填結果。

en.summary: Turn “more efficient” into observable measures, label assumptions and data sources, and connect requirement changes with test evidence and subsequent decisions.
objectives: Define observable success conditions for both program behavior and user tasks.
Specify denominators, measurement methods, baselines and scope for metrics.
Bring assumptions, proposed requirements, confirmed decisions and revision reasons back to problem.md.

readingGuide.goal: Define observable success conditions for both program behavior and user tasks.
readingGuide.startingPoint: problem.md, a text editor and this lesson’s synthetic arithmetic. Do not collect actual participant scores or timing.
readingGuide.route: Read the scenario and principles, compare examples, then expand problem.md and use the checks to review your understanding.
readingGuide.output: Reproducible metric definitions, assumptions, proposed requirements and change records in problem.md, with results honestly left unmeasured.

sections.heading: How will you judge whether the system helps?
paragraphs: This lesson determines whether the system you build merely runs or actually solves the problem.
Remember this principle: delivering a feature does not establish that a goal has been achieved. Achievement needs evidence, and you must define how to obtain that evidence beforehand.
Imagine spending a month developing an AI system and reporting to your manager:
“We completed 20 features, wrote 10,000 lines of code, and the AI can generate reports automatically!”
Your manager might ask just one question:
“How much faster is the work that used to take half an hour? Have errors decreased?”
That is the core question for today.

sections.heading: 1. Connect Requirements with Evidence
paragraphs: First, connect the parts of the software development process.

blocks.caption: Figure 1 | From problem to decision
blocks.description: Six steps connect requirements, design hypotheses, metrics and evidence; evidence may call for revision.

items.title: 1. Problem
items.body: Users often omit information, causing report errors.

items.title: 2. Requirement
items.body: Missing data must prevent complete-report export.

items.title: 3. Hypothesis
items.body: Telling users what is missing may help them correct it independently.

items.title: 4. Metric
items.body: Missing-input blocking rate, unprompted completion rate, completion time.

items.title: 5. Evidence
items.body: Test records, observed task results and error cases.

items.title: 6. Decision
items.body: Accept, revise the design or revisit the requirements.

paragraphs: The crucial distinction is that requirements specify what a system should do; hypotheses explain why a design might work; metrics define how to judge the outcome.
Keep these three concepts distinct.

sections.heading: 2. Functional and Task Metrics: System Success and User Success
paragraphs: Suppose you are developing an AI document-intake system.
Users upload documents, the system checks for missing items, and it generates a report.
How can you tell whether it works well?
You need two perspectives.

blocks.caption: Figure 2 | Functional and task metrics
blocks.description: Obtain these two complementary evidence types separately.

items.title: Functional Metric
items.body:
Does the system behave correctly under the specified rules?

Examples: does missing input block export? Do edits require a new check?

Typical methods: automated tests and manual functional tests.

items.title: Task Metric
items.body:
Can users complete the work they actually need to do?

Example: can a first-time user locate omissions, supply the missing data and obtain a correct report independently?

Methods can include user task tests, timing and observation.

paragraphs: Why must these metrics be recorded separately?
Imagine a system with a “Check for missing items” button.
Engineers find that every click performs the check correctly: the functional metric reaches 100%.
Actual users, however, cannot find the button.
In that situation:

- The feature may pass its engineering test.
- The user's task may still fail.
The reverse also holds. A user successfully generating one report does not establish that the system has passed every safety and exception check.
A useful system needs evidence both that its behavior is correct and that users can accomplish their tasks.

sections.heading: 3. Calculate Success Metrics: The Denominator Matters
paragraphs: Now work through the arithmetic.
Suppose there are six synthetic test records: four have missing information and two are complete.
The measure we want is the missing-input blocking rate.
Formula: missing-input blocking rate = successfully blocked missing-input cases / all missing-input cases × 100%.

blocks.caption: Figure 3 | Explore the number of blocked cases
blocks.description: Four fixed synthetic missing-input cases; the calculation is practice rather than actual test evidence.

items.title: Blocking requirement not met
items.body: This version requires all 4 / 4 cases to be blocked.

items.title: Interpretation
items.body: One missing-input case remains unblocked. Successful complete-input cases do not make this rule pass.

sections.heading: Denominators, zero cases and overblocking
paragraphs: Remember three points.
First, the denominator must match the target of your question. We are asking whether missing input is blocked, so the denominator is the four incomplete records, rather than all six.
Second, percentages cannot replace raw counts. Although 75% may sound acceptable, 3/4 exposes the one missed case. This fails the particular acceptance requirement.
Third, no test does not mean success. If there are no missing-input cases, the denominator is zero and the rate cannot be calculated. Record “not measured / not applicable” rather than 100%.
There is another trap: blocking all six records also produces a missing-input blocking rate of 100%, while preventing complete records from being processed.
Pair this metric with functional tests such as whether complete data can be exported correctly, so that optimizing one number does not prevent useful work.

sections.heading: 4. Establish Whether Users Really Finish Faster
paragraphs: Suppose an AI product claims:
“Our product saves five minutes when producing a report.”
Your first question should be:
How were those five minutes measured?
Consider two timing methods.

blocks.caption: Figure 4 | Check the timing boundaries
blocks.description: The illustrative 15 and 10 minutes cover different intervals and do not establish a five-minute saving.

items.title: Old workflow
items.body:
15 minutes

Timing starts at opening documents and organizing data.

items.title: New workflow
items.body:
10 minutes

Timing starts only after data preparation, at pressing Generate.

paragraphs: The apparent saving is five minutes, but the workflows use different starting points.
That comparison is unfair.
Use the same task, data of comparable difficulty, and matching start and end conditions as far as possible. Record whether users receive additional assistance.
For example, define the interval as:
“From the first time the user sees the assigned data until they obtain a correct report matching the current data.”
Even with that definition, consider this:
If a user tries the old system first and the new system second, they may finish faster simply because they now know the task.
This is the practice effect.

A single observed time difference therefore cannot establish that the new system caused the improvement. A stronger comparison can vary workflow order across participants or use different tasks of equivalent difficulty.
Timing only successful participants also creates a problem. If half abandon the task, you cannot report the mean time of the successful half without disclosing the failures.

sections.heading: 5. Hypotheses: Beliefs Need Testing
paragraphs: This distinction matters especially in AI development.
To help users correct their own data, suppose you design this feature:
“When information is missing, display the names of the missing fields.”
You expect users to fill in the information themselves.
But remember:
This is a design hypothesis, not an established fact.
It may fail for several reasons.
Users may not understand the field name. They may know what is missing but not where to get it. They may know the source but lack permission to access it.
Turn the idea into a statement that can be tested.

blocks.caption: Table 2
rows: Explicitly listing missing fields helps users correct their own data
Ask users to complete an assigned correction task without hints
Unprompted completion rate, where users get stuck and why
Users understand the message but repeatedly cannot find the source data
Investigate how data is obtained or improve the feedback design

paragraphs: The disconfirming condition is particularly useful.
It asks:
What result would make me willing to revise the original idea?
Scientific research and engineering verification share this question.
A research paper proposes a hypothesis, obtains evidence through experiments, and then draws a conclusion.
Software engineering follows the same logic, with evidence potentially coming from functional tests, user task tests or operational data.

sections.heading: 6. Requirement Records: Preserve the Reason for Changes
paragraphs: The final core concept is traceability: being able to follow a requirement back to its source and decisions.
Imagine this development situation.
The original requirement says:
“Users may export a report after completing the data check.”
The engineer implements the feature.
Testing then reveals a problem.

blocks.caption: Figure 5 | The stale check-result problem
blocks.description: Design risk: the final proposed rule addresses this risk; acceptance evidence is still pending.

items.title: 1. Check data A
items.body: The user enters data A, runs the check and receives a pass.

items.title: 2. Edit to data B
items.body: The user edits the input, producing data B.

items.title: 3. Retain the old status
items.body: The system keeps the “check passed” status for data A.

items.title: 4. Export without rechecking
items.body: The user exports a report for data B without a new check.

items.title: Rule to add
items.body: Whenever input affecting the check changes, invalidate the old pass status. Require a new check before complete-report export.

paragraphs: This is a common type of problem.
The original requirement may be incomplete without being wrong.
Instead of silently overwriting the original, record:

blocks.caption: Table 3
rows: Missing items must prevent complete-report export
Clear missing-input feedback helps users correct data independently
Every specified missing-input case must be blocked
Input edits invalidate the previous check result
A stale check result could otherwise allow export
Testing pending; no evidence obtained yet

paragraphs: Why is this table useful?
Three months later, a new engineer may ask: “Why must users check again every time they edit the data?”
The record points to the original requirement, discovered risk, decision rationale, and the test that verifies the rule.
This is requirements traceability. It supports long-term maintenance as well as document management.
H, M, R and C are demonstration category codes in this lesson, rather than a mandatory standard.

sections.heading: 7. Start Applying This with One Document
paragraphs: An MVP does not necessarily need a large requirements-management system.
Start with a Markdown file named problem.md that holds the essential information together.

Here is a compact example. The Chinese template is preserved identically in both editions; it records the problem, R-01, unverified H-01, M-01/M-02 with their denominators and unmeasured results, C-01 with its reason, and pending evidence.

blocks.heading: problem.md
paragraphs: Synthetic example; results remain unmeasured.
blocks.code:
# AI 文件收件系統

## 問題
使用者常因資料缺漏，產生不完整報告。

## 需求 R-01
缺件時不得完整匯出報告。

## 假設 H-01
顯示缺漏欄位可以協助使用者自行修正。

狀態：尚未驗證

## 功能指標 M-01
名稱：缺漏阻擋率
公式：阻擋成功數 / 指定缺漏案例數
要求：指定案例全數阻擋
結果：未測量

## 任務指標 M-02
名稱：無提示完成率
公式：無提示完成者 / 開始任務者
結果：未測量

## 變更 C-01
修改輸入後，舊檢查結果必須失效。

理由：避免以過期結果匯出。

## 待補證據
- 功能測試結果
- 使用者測試紀錄
- 驗收決策

paragraphs: In the template, the problem is incomplete reports caused by missing data. R-01 prohibits complete-report export when required items are missing. H-01 proposes that naming missing fields will help users correct data themselves; its status remains unverified. M-01 names the blocking rate, divides successful blocks by specified missing-input cases and requires all those cases to be blocked; its result remains unmeasured. M-02 divides unprompted completions by everyone who starts the task; its result also remains unmeasured. C-01 invalidates the old check after an input edit, to prevent export based on stale results. Functional test results, user test records and the acceptance decision are still needed. The document's value comes from the questions it answers, rather than its field count.
Anyone opening it should be able to tell:
“What problem are we solving? What do we currently believe? How will we judge success? What has actually been tested? Why are we making a change?”
That makes the document useful during development, acceptance and maintenance.

sections.heading: 8. Place This Lesson in the Wider Engineering Process
paragraphs: Think of M03-05 as a bridge between requirements engineering and software testing.

blocks.caption: Table 4
rows: How will we judge its performance?
How do we obtain reliable results?
Where did each rule come from?
What happens when results differ from expectations?

paragraphs: Distinguish three frequently confused terms:
Verification: did we build the system correctly according to the specified requirements?
Validation: does the system meet the real needs of users doing their work?
Evaluation: measuring system performance and limitations using defined metrics and methods.
Correctly identifying missing input is important verification evidence. Users successfully completing correction tasks can provide validation evidence.
These evidence types complement one another, and each requires more than an unsupported claim.

sections.heading: 9. Check Your Understanding
paragraphs: This is a new synthetic scenario. Try answering first; the questions stay visible here, and reference answers can be expanded in “Understanding checks and reference explanations” below.
A hospital is testing an AI document-checking system.
Engineers prepare five missing-input cases. Four are blocked, but one still allows export.
Four participants start the task: two finish independently, one needs a staff hint, and one abandons it.
The project manager claims: “We expect to save each user eight minutes, so the system already has value for release.”
Answer these questions:

1. What is the missing-input blocking rate? Does it pass a requirement that every specified missing-input case be blocked?
2. What is the unprompted completion rate? Should the person needing a hint remain in the denominator?
3. Is “saving eight minutes” currently a hypothesis, a measured result, or a formal conclusion? How would you verify it?
4. If input edits leave the previous check result active, what requirement would you add? What change records would you retain?
The lesson's main point is to provide reliable, relevant evidence that the original problem has improved, rather than counting activities completed.
Next, M04-01 introduces HCI, UI and UX. Today's question—whether users can complete their tasks—supports the later work on user experience design and usability testing.

exercise.environment: problem.md, a text editor and this lesson’s synthetic arithmetic. Do not collect actual participant scores or timing.
steps: Choose one functional and one task metric. Define denominators, start/end conditions, sources and unmeasured fields.
Calculate the synthetic result with four missing-input cases and three blocked exports. Explain why complete inputs are excluded and handle a zero denominator separately.
Add H-01, R-01 and one change with sources, confirming role and reason. Ask a peer to identify the next claim needing verification.
exercise.expected: Reproducible metric definitions, assumptions, proposed requirements and change records in problem.md, with results honestly left unmeasured.
exercise.check: Calculate 3/4 = 75% and identify failure to meet this version’s blocking requirement. Do not treat synthetic arithmetic as actual participant or software results.
exercise.cleanup: Retain synthetic labels and original definitions. Do not publish actual participant task records. Keep unmeasured items unmeasured.

openChecks.prompt: What is the blocking rate, and does it meet the all-cases requirement?
answer: 4/5 = 80%. One missing-input case is incorrectly allowed through, so the requirement that every specified case be blocked is not met.

openChecks.prompt: What is the unprompted completion rate? Does the prompted user remain in the denominator?
answer: 2/4 = 50%. All four people who start remain in the denominator, including the prompted participant and the person who abandons. The prompted participant is excluded from the unprompted-success numerator.

openChecks.prompt: What status does “saving eight minutes” have, and how would you test it?
answer: It is a hypothesis about expected improvement, with no measured result yet. Fix tasks, comparable data and start/end conditions; record assistance, failures and abandonment. Consider varying workflow order to address practice effects before comparing the baseline and new workflow.

openChecks.prompt: What rule and records address a stale result after edits?
answer: Invalidate the previous pass whenever input affecting the check changes, and require a new check before complete-report export. Retain the original requirement, C-01, rationale, sources, decision and pending acceptance evidence; add actual results after testing.
